name: Andrés Duarte Ornelas
tagline: Cybersecurity graduate student and engineer specializing in network security architecture, incident response, and the intersection of LLMs with cybersecurity
summary: Cybersecurity graduate student pursuing a dual Master's in Cybersecurity between UTSA and Tecnológico de Monterrey, with hands-on experience in network security architecture, vulnerability assessment, incident response, and digital forensics. Experienced in designing segmented network architectures, conducting vulnerability assessments, and researching the application of LLMs in autonomous network operations.

highlights: Evaluated risks in production environments and developed tailored mitigation solutions
Designed and implemented segmented office network using VLANs with DMZ for internet-facing services
Configured traffic rules to control inter-segment communication and enhance network security
Performed web vulnerability scanning using Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP) to identify and remediate threats
Assisted in creating and implementing company-wide cybersecurity policy framework
Gained hands-on experience in security incident management and response
Conducted comprehensive vulnerability assessments and implemented system hardening strategies
Documented security findings and provided actionable recommendations to enhance cybersecurity posture

projects.name: Empirical Characterization of a Commercial Coding Agent for CLI-Based OSPF Fault Diagnosis
projects.description: Conducted the first empirical evaluation of a general-purpose coding agent (Claude Code) performing autonomous OSPF fault diagnosis in a traditional, non-SDN CLI environment, addressing a gap in existing LLM network operations research.
highlights: Designed a 50-session quantitative experiment using a three-router GNS3/VyOS topology modeled after CCNA 11.6.3, with six simultaneously active faults per session and automated pre/post verification via Netmiko snapshots
Achieved an effective fault resolution rate of ~97% and a perfect-run rate of ~78% at a mean cost of $0.81/session; zero sessions introduced a configuration regression
Publicly released experimental materials, router configurations, and analysis scripts at github.com/Doarte45/LLMnetopsLab

projects.name: Cloud as a Service Commercial and Operative Design
projects.description: Designed multi-cloud service architecture using AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud for company Quanti. Developed commercial strategy for service delivery and operational framework.

projects.name: Digital Forensic Investigation: "Posthumous Digital Note" Case Analysis
projects.description: Collaborated on comprehensive digital forensic analysis of suspicious death case using industry-standard tools (Autopsy/Sleuth Kit, Volatility, Registry Explorer). Analyzed disk images, RAM dumps, and Windows event logs to reconstruct timeline and establish evidence of third-party involvement. Documented complete chain of custody following ISO/IEC 27037 and NIST SP 800-86 standards.
